This discharges step (i) of ctr-0004, open since cycle 27. open_questions[5] says src-0017's evaluator matches 'with a SUBSTRING rule in both directions'. IT DOES NOT. The EXECUTING code in stage3_ti_drafting/ioc/eval/eval_ioc.py is ONE-DIRECTIONAL, verbatim: 'true_positives = sum(any(pred.lower() in gt.lower() for gt in gt_set) for pred in pred_list)', with 'false_positives = len(pred_list) - true_positives' and 'false_negatives = sum(not any(pred.lower() in gt.lower() for pred in pred_list) for gt in gt_set)'. The two-directional variant and the exact-match variant are EACH ENCLOSED IN A TRIPLE-QUOTED STRING LITERAL and never execute; the comment lines cycle 21 quoted are the headers standing above those dead blocks. THE SOURCE STATES THE SAME RULE IN ITS OWN PROSE -- IoC sub-README, verbatim: 'A prediction is considered a True Positive (TP) if pred.lower() in gt.lower() for any ground truth IOC from the same source'. Code and documentation agree with each other and against what this issue said. THE CONSEQUENCE IS AN ASYMMETRIC BIAS, NOT A ONE-WAY ONE. The rule is LENIENT toward short or fragmentary predictions, since any prediction that is a substring of a longer ground-truth entry scores TP. It is STRICT against verbose predictions, since a prediction containing the ground-truth IoC plus surrounding text scores a FALSE POSITIVE -- and that is the characteristic failure mode of a free-form LLM extractor, i.e. exactly the case the dead two-directional block would have scored TP. A verbose-but-correct prediction is moreover penalised TWICE, as a false positive AND as a false negative, because the ground-truth entry it contains is simultaneously left unmatched by the false_negatives line above. So the limitation recorded at src-0017.md, that 'A substring-permissive matcher inflates true positives relative to strict equality', is HALF RIGHT and must never be repeated unqualified: relative to strict equality this matcher INFLATES on one axis and DEFLATES on the other, and THE NET SIGN IS UNKNOWN because it is the difference of two unmeasured quantities. PARTIAL MITIGATION, recorded so the deflation is not over-read: both sides pass through the same normalisation chain (transcribed verbatim in ctr-0004), which strips defanging -- hxxp to http, bracket removal -- and truncates at the first ' - ' separator, so the commonest verbose-prediction artefacts in CTI text are normalised away BEFORE matching. What survives the chain as verbose FP is free prose around the indicator, and a URL-with-path predicted against a bare-domain ground truth. WHAT REMAINS GENUINELY OPEN: the net sign and magnitude of the bias. It cannot be recovered without the per-model prediction files, which are now confirmed ABSENT from both release mirrors -- see open_questions[7].
